SELECTED_INDEX: 9  
CONFIDENCE: 0.27  
EXPLANATION:  
• The strong doublet at 742 / 733 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the symmetric CF₂ (or CF₃-like) stretching/rocking modes often seen for –CF₂– or –CF₃ substituents attached to unsaturated centres; candidate 9 (FC(F)=C(F)P, i.e. CF₂=CF–PH₂) is the only molecule that contains a –CF₂– group able to give such intense Raman bands.  
• The band at 999 cm⁻¹ matches the P–H bending (ν₂ of PH₂/PH₃ analogues), consistent with GFQ-007 (970–1010 cm⁻¹). Candidate 9 uniquely possesses P–H bonds; none of the other candidates have any P–H or Si-H bonds that could account for this peak.  
• The 607 cm⁻¹ line agrees with a typical P–C stretching / CF₂ bending region (600–650 cm⁻¹), fitting the P–C bond present only in candidate 9.  
• The weak band at 2980 cm⁻¹ indicates C–H stretching (GFQ-003). Candidate 9 is the single candidate that actually contains a C–H bond (on the vinyl carbon), whereas the other fluorinated/chlorinated species are completely hydrogen-free.  
• The medium feature at 1217 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to C–F stretching in a CF₂= moiety, again matching candidate 9’s structure.  

Taken together, the simultaneous presence of CF₂ vibrations, P–H bending, a P–C bond, and a C–H stretch is only compatible with candidate 9. Therefore it is the best match to the experimental Raman spectrum.
